newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady to firmer,Mideast active.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady to firmer,Mideast active.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates for Very Large and Ultra Large Crude Carriers (ULCCs and VLCCs) sailing from the Mideast to Japan were steady to firmer in active trade on Monday, brokers said.
Rates in other regions were mostly stable although slower trade to Singapore and thinning cross Med business saw rates for these routes marked slightly softer.

Vela added two further ULCCs to the 500,000 tonne Kapetan Michalis fixed on Friday at W42.5 for voyage to the U.S. Gulf. One, the Stena King with 450,000 tonnes at the same level and one the Tina for 350,000 tonnes at W45.
Rates for 250,000 tonne VLCCs were holding firm around W62.5 against 1997 worldscale rates after jumping around five worldscale points last week in active trade.
Trade from the Mideast to the Far East remained active and rates held steady but slower trade to Singapore saw rates slip 2.5 points to around W50.
West African rates held steady in active transatlantic trade for Suezmax tonnage although the Argoaftis was booked at the slightly lower rate of W81.
Slower cross Mediterranean activity saw rates for Suezmax cargoes off around five points at W105.
Activity in the UK/Cont region was also thin but rates for 80,000 tonne cargoes were holding around W108.
